case_name: Jayamadhavan vs Sumi S on 30 July, 2016
facts_of_case: Petitioner and respondent are husband and wife. Petitioner sought a decree of divorce under Section 13(I)(ib) and IA(ii) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Trial court dismissed the petition.

legal_principles.principle: Either party to a marriage has the right to present a petition for dissolution of the marriage on the ground that there has been no restitution of conjugal rights between the parties for a period of one year after the passing of a decree for restitution of conjugal rights.
legal_principles.held: A perusal of the above makes it clear that either party to a marriage whether solemnised before or after the commencement of the Act has a right to present a petition for the dissolution of a marriage on the ground that there has been no restitution of conjugal rights between the parties to the marriage for a period of one year after the passing of the decree for restitution of conjugal rights.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party alleging desertion to prove it.
legal_principles.held: According to the Family Court, the allegation of desertion made by the petitioner has not been proved.

outcome.final_order: Family Court's decision to dismiss the petition is set aside. A decree of divorce may be granted under Section 13(1A)(ii) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
